title: Basis of Subscription and Seat Licence Billing on a Corporate Travel Programme
content:
Under the Corporate Travel Programmes, the platform subscription on a programme is charged in advance for each billing period at the tier's monthly rate, or at its annual rate where the company is invoiced yearly; the two are never both charged.

## The seat licence for a period

Seats beyond those included in the tier are charged at the tier's seat licence rate for each seat for each month of the period, counted on the seats contracted rather than the seats actually assigned. The seats charged are the seats contracted less the seats the tier includes, and where the seats contracted do not exceed the seats included the number charged is nothing at all. That number of seats is multiplied by the tier's monthly seat licence rate, for each month of the period.

## A period that is not a whole month

A period that begins or ends part way through a month is charged pro rata by whole days out of the days in that month.

## Falling due, interest and the credit limit

Invoices fall due within the tier's payment terms counted from the invoice date, and an overdue balance carries the tier's monthly interest from the day after it falls due. A programme whose unpaid balance passes the tier's credit limit is suspended rather than allowed to book further.

## Invoicing currency

Where the company elects to be invoiced in a currency other than the contract currency, the tier's conversion markup is added to each invoice.

## What the programme's balance means

The balance on a Corporate Travel Programme is the net amount billed to the contracting company: subscriptions, seat licences, transaction fees, overage and interest credit the account, and credit notes and rebates debit it. Each billing period raises a line for the subscription and a line for each seat licence, carrying the first and last dates of the period charged, the currency the line was invoiced in and the invoice it was billed under.

## Worked illustration, on hypothetical figures

Take a programme contracting 14 seats, on a tier that carries 8 seats in its subscription and licences each further seat at 5.00 USD for each month. The seats charged are 14 less 8, that is 6 seats. Six seats multiplied by 5.00 USD is 30.00 USD of seat licence for a whole month of the period. Where the period runs over only 10 whole days of a month of 31 days, that month's charge is taken pro rata by 10 whole days out of the 31 days in that month.

A second hypothetical: the same programme contracts 8 seats. The seats contracted do not exceed the seats the tier carries, so the seats charged are nothing at all and no seat licence arises for that period, whatever number of those seats has actually been assigned to named travellers.
